candidates.heuristic_context: Target problem types: delays caused by batch processing or periodic handling of cases, accumulation of waiting cases before execution. Applicable structural situations: activities executed in batches or triggered periodically instead of being processed immediately when a case arrives. How the data is used: Repeated patterns where multiple cases start the same activity at nearly identical timestamps or where long waiting times precede activity execution indicate batch or periodic processing instead of case-by-case handling. Transformation style: redesign the process so that cases are processed individually upon arrival instead of waiting for batch or periodic execution. Feasibility: Yes. Batch patterns and periodic execution behavior can be detected from event log timestamps, and the process can be redesigned to enable case-by-case execution.
candidates.additional_context:
This candidate consolidates batching signals from 4 observations on different events that all causally trace back to the W_ work activity 'W_Nabellen offertes'. Source A_/O_ events: 'O_CANCELLED', 'O_SENT_BACK', 'A_CANCELLED'. The evidence fields below are the strongest single observation (most negative arrival_execution_gap). A single CBW redesign on this W_ target captures the full merged signal.

The execution rate meets or exceeds the arrival rate, suggesting that case-by-case processing is feasible without additional capacity. The average batch size is 273.5 cases, which is large. Transitioning to case-by-case processing would significantly change the workload pattern for this activity. This activity exhibits rework in 4274 cases (32.7% of all cases). Rework in a batched activity may indicate that batch errors propagate across multiple cases. Whether batch execution can be replaced by case-by-case processing depends on system scheduling policies, operational constraints (e.g. external system availability windows), and whether downstream systems require batched input — none of which can be determined from the event log alone.
